deck: Table Rock this morning: 910.67 ft. Taneycomo still eats on a pink worm if the generators give you a window.

play.title: Streamer on the generate.
play.body: When SWPA spins it, Taneycomo becomes a small river. A dark wooly bugger in the seams.

season.name: Fall turnover
season.why: The lake turns over and the fish don't read the same book they did in August. Crankbaits get good again. Trout streamers get good. This is the season Branson locals wait for.
tips: Windblown banks and shad-colored cranks, 8–18 feet.
Walleye on the same gravel they used all summer, just shallower.
Taneycomo: streamers and wooly buggers when they generate. Hoppers until the first frost.
A jacket in the boat. Dawn is cold before the strip is.

tomorrow: Tomorrow we print a new level, a new play, and whether the dam spun overnight. Open it before you drive. The water will have moved.
weekGraf: The pool walked down from 910.90 early in the week to 910.67 this morning — about 0.23 ft off that earlier mark, still under the 915 full pool. Ramps are still in. Shallow coves feel a falling pool first.

now.temp: Verify at the ramp — scout does not invent dawn temps
now.clarity: Clear near the dam; arms can stain. Verify locally.

body: With the lake just over 4 feet below full pool, more shoreline, stumps, and hazards are exposed in the shallow coves, creek arms, and near some ramps. Take it slow up the James, Kings, and Long Creek arms, and check your launch point.

Surface water has cooled into the upper 60s with gin-clear visibility. Bass respond well to topwaters and soft plastics early, then shift to jigs, live bait, or drop-shot rigs around long points, gravel flats dropping into 20–40 feet, and offshore structure. Mixed-bag action includes walleye holding on points in 20–25 feet and crappie or spotted bass coming from deeper brush and around docks. Recent patterns show solid catches when presentations stay clean in this clear, cooling water.

taneycomo.dek: Cold tailwater · generation is the whole game

now.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F below the dam). Verify at the bank.
now.generation: ~306 cfs on the last printed reading. Not a live hourly. Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad.

body: This cold tailwater stays productive year-round thanks to deep releases from Table Rock and steady stocking. Generation remains the primary tactic book: minimal or low flows early create excellent windows for wading, light-line drifting, or indicator fishing with micro jigs, midges, scuds, worms, or Gulp eggs, while stronger current (often building in the afternoon and evening) calls for weighted rigs and precise drifts through seams and behind structure.

From Table Rock Dam down to Fall Creek is trophy water — artificial lures and flies only; no soft plastics or scented/natural baits. Rainbows 12–20 inches must be released. Save pink worms, PowerBait, Gulp eggs or other soft plastics/scented baits for the water below Fall Creek. A trout permit is required in many areas. Recent reports (Oct 20 Lilleys journal and Oct tackle.net) highlight slow dock fishing but better boat catches on worms and eggs, very good wading with Pink PowerWorm when off, and a notable 28.25-inch rainbow. Water clarity is good to murky in places — clean, natural presentations win. Call 866-494-1993 for the latest SWPA schedule before you wade.
